newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close down, TELCO rises.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close down, TELCO rises.

text.p: Strong buying in automobile maker TELCO failed to lift Delhi share prices on Wednesday as investors stayed on the sidelines, awaiting an imminent increase in petroleum products prices, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 2.36 points lower at 758.99 points.
Shares of TELCO, which announced its 1996/97 (April-March) corporate results on Tuesday, closed 1.95 rupees higher at 395.95.
TELCO's 1996/97 net profit increased to 7.62 billion rupees from 5.30 billion in the previous year.

"Deferred hike in petroleum prices and a slowdown in buying by foreign institutional investors following sluggish market conditions continued to dampen buying," said Surinder Gulati of brokers Share Academy.
On Sunday, strong resistance by left-wing parties prevented the ruling United Front from reaching a consensus to raise the prices of some oil products to manage a growing oil subsidy bill.
Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral has promised to take a bold decision to tackle mounting losses due to a government subsidy paid to oil firms.
Hero Honda Motors inched up 0.75 rupee to 482.25 on selective buying, brokers said. On Tuesday the company announced a 91 percent increase in its 1996/97 (April-March) profit.
Larsen and Toubro dropped 3.75 rupees to 204.00.
